name_reason: Compliant with fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=chapter, descriptor=17_init. The '17' is a meaningful chapter ID (chapters 01-30 are domain IDs), not a Ghidra address residue (function address 0x335AA != 17). Dispatched from data_fd2_chapter_init_handler_table (DATA xref from 0x51db1, 0 direct callers); all sibling handlers share the fd2_chapter_NN_init naming. Name accurately reflects the per-chapter init purpose.
purpose: Chapter 17 (血與冰之刃) per-chapter init handler: re-inits battle state, conditionally loads portrait set 1 only when 蜜蒂 (char id 0x12) is absent from the party, plays dialog page 0, and pans the camera to char 0.
logic_summary: 1) fd2_init_battle_state_for_chapter(). 2) if fd2_check_party_has_char_id(0x12) == 0 (蜜蒂 NOT in party) then fd2_load_chapter_portraits_and_dump_tmp(1). 3) fd2_display_dialog_scene(data_fd2_current_chapter_text, 0, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xcd, 0x4c, 0x4a, 0x13, 1) -- dialog page 0. 4) fd2_pan_cursor_to_char(0). The leading __CHK(0x28) is the Watcom frame-size stack-probe, not source. In the binary the dialog+pan tail is a tail-JMP into the shared page-0 dialog chain (0x3344D -> 0x33206 -> 0x33140) owned by chapters 12/07/05; src is the functionally-equivalent Layer-2 straight-line form.

returns.semantics: No return value; init handler invoked via the chapter init handler dispatch table for its side effects.

comment_original_issue: Existing source comment block was accurate, precise, and well-structured (correctly described the data-dependent portrait load gated on 蜜蒂 absence, the genuine TEST EAX,EAX/JNZ, the __CHK(0x28) note, the tail-JMP Layer-2 sharing chain, and linked handlers). Only issue: three em-dash characters (U+2014) violated the ASCII-only-for-comments rule; replaced with '--'. No semantic change.
notes: Plate comment at 0x335AA is a condensed version consistent with the refined source understanding (correctly states __CHK(0x28), conditional portrait load on 蜜蒂 absence, dialog page 0, pan to char 0, linked End/Post-action handlers); left unchanged. Other em-dashes remain elsewhere in chinit.c (other symbols' comment blocks) and are intentionally out of scope per the strict one-symbol rule.
